## Pipeline rule
The user does not code: I build, they direct and look. **Python tools do the work and export JSON + GLB; Bevy is a thin loader.** New features are data plus small Rust.
- `py tools/export_scene.py <town run folder> <glb dir> [out=assets]` writes `assets/scene/avalon.json` and copies the GLBs it uses into `assets/models` (34 now).
- **Frame conversion:** Unreal II is X/Y ground, Z up, 50 units per metre, left-handed. Bevy = `(x/50, z/50, y/50)`, yaw negated. That is one reflection, so the town renders the same, not mirrored. Whether the buildings really face the roads is still unverified.
- The JSON holds:
  - `terrain`: 128x128 heights, row j along +Z;
  - `sea_y`, `start` (the summit) and `start_yaw`;
  - `instances` `{mesh, pos, yaw, scale}`;
  - `placeholders` for stock Unreal meshes we cannot ship, drawn as primitives;
  - `missing`: meshes without a GLB.
- Bevy 0.20 renames to remember: SceneRoot → WorldAssetRoot, AmbientLight → GlobalAmbientLight. Observers use `On<Add<T>>`, scenes use `bsn_list!`, shaders are WESL. Hot reload is the `file_watcher` feature. For headless runs, disable WinitPlugin and add ScheduleRunnerPlugin, or use MinimalPlugins.

---

<!-- skilltree -->
> Skill tree: this file is the overview. Each `->` line points to the full section in `tree/`; Read only the branch the task needs.
## Scope
-> `tree/01-scope.md` (~280t): Run the Avalon town story simulation (storysim.py) - citizens as local Gemma agents, important characters on the big tier (claude), and the ...

## Command
```
py tools/storysim.py [days=3] [out=<dir>] [resume=<dir>] [small=URL] [big=URL|claude] [dm=claude|URL] [step=60] [only=a,b] [backend=live|dry] [model_dm=opus] [think_big=0|1]
```
- `backend=dry` first: it checks the binder, routines and places without a model. Then `live`.
- `only=a,b` limits to named citizens for a quick test; `resume=<dir>` continues a run (memories and nudges reload).
- `step=60` = minutes per turn; an in-game DAY is 06:00-23:00.

## The three tiers
| Tier | Who | Engine |
|---|---|---|
| SMALL | the 22 ordinary citizens | Gemma 4 12B QAT on llama-server :8081 (`small=http://127.0.0.1:8081`) |
| BIG | hawkins, rook, oduya, nkemelu, okafor, marau | `big=claude` (`claude -p`); Pantheon 26B was deleted, so no local big tier exists |
| DRAMA MANAGER | the writer, once per in-game day | `dm=claude model_dm=opus` |

The drama manager: vetoes and retcons lines that break canon; at most 3 nudges per day; private urges for idle characters; rewrites each character's memory summary; schedules beats (`catwalk`, `supply_drop`, `census`, `drain_lamp`). It never writes a citizen's line itself.

## Per-turn safety net (`check_turn`)
Every citizen turn must be valid JSON, name a known place, respect the citizen's routine, keep the line short and invent no people. On failure: retry at lower temperature, then fall back to the routine action. Keep this; it is what made 22 small agents usable.

## Outputs
`log.jsonl` (every turn), `day_N.md` (readable day), `memories.json`, `nudges.json`, `story.md` (the writer's compiled story). Story hooks worth keeping go to `U2Avalon/tools/HOOKS.md`.

## Servers and the GPU (rules from `local-gpu-ai`)
1. Check the card first (`nvidia-smi`, running python/llama processes); announce on the GPU protocol to the other live chats.
2. `bash Documents/Tools/llm/start_servers.sh small` (Gemma, `-c 16384 -np 4 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`); ~3 min to load, ~8 GB. 24K context spilled the card: stay at 16K.
3. Run; then ALWAYS `bash Documents/Tools/llm/stop_servers.sh` and confirm VRAM freed. Servers hold VRAM while idle.

---
name: drawing-to-level
description: "Top-down level map drawing to Blender blockout + level analysis (sightlines, reveal, isovists); scores Avalon layouts"
---

## Scope
Turn the user's top-down level map drawing (houses, trees, path arrows, landmark, camera arrows) into a 3D Blender blockout rendered from the drawn cameras, then score it as a level - landmark visibility along the path, first reveal, squeeze/release (isovists via pysovist), clearance, winding, leading lines - with an overlay drawn on the user's own sketch. Also scores any generated layout (Avalon towns) given in the same layout.json format. Use for "make my level map 3D", "analyse this level", "is the landmark visible", sightline/isovist checks.

# Drawing -> 3D level + level analysis (built 2026-10-12, PC chat, page3; the user: "that is perfect")

First run: `Documents/U2Golem/scenefit/page3/` (scans `IMG_20261012_0001.jpg` map, `_0002.jpg` mansion front).
Scripts (copies of the page3 ones) are in `scripts/` here. Run them from the level's own folder.

## 1. Read the map into layout.json (by hand, ~15 min)
- Rotate the scan upright -> `map_up.png`; thumbnail to 1400 wide with a 50 px grid -> `map_grid.png`.
- Read every object off the grid into `layout.json` (grid px; `scale_m_per_px` 0.1 for page3; y down = north/uphill):
  ```
  buildings [[cx,cy,w,h,angle_deg_clockwise], ...]   round_C [cx,cy,r]   mansion_A [cx,cy,w,h,angle]
  trees [[x,y],...]   path [[x,y],...] (in walking order)   cameras [[x,y,dx,dy],...] (drawn C1 arrows)
  hill {top:[x,y], height_m, radius_px}   edge_labels {A2:[x,y],...}   map_box [x0,y0,x1,y1]
  ```
- Edge labels (A2, B3...) are links to neighbouring sheets; keep them.

## 2. Cards from the drawings
`scripts/cut_cards.py` (Hunyuan venv python `-I`): alpha card per drawn tree / side view / landmark front. Mask = gray < thr (110; 120 for the mansion),
MORPH_CLOSE grow 9 (15), keep parts > 0.2% of the area, flood-fill the inside so the pencil inside stays. Crops are in layout.json `cuts_preview_px`.

## 3. Blockout
`"/c/Program Files/Blender Foundation/"*/blender.exe -b --factory-startup -P build_level.py -- <folder>` (~6 s, CPU/EEVEE):
hill = `H*max(0,1-d/R)^2`, path strip, leaning boxes 5-8 m + pyramid roofs, C cylinder + dome, crossed tree cards,
landmark card 16 m tall, dusk sun. Renders `renders/cam1..n` (drawn cameras, 1.7 m eye), `top` (ortho), `overview`; saves `level_blockout.blend`.
Contact sheet: PIL, 3x2 at 640x360 -> `renders/sheet.jpg`.

## 4. Analysis
`py -3.13 -I analyze_level.py <folder>` (pysovist 0.1.2 MIT + shapely 2.2, installed for py 3.13) -> `analysis.json` + `analysis_overlay.png`.
Path sampled every 2 m. Per sample: landmark seen (2D, free line to any of 9 points on it), A seen in 3D (eye 1.7 m, worst-case 8 m roofs, the hill),
isovist area / r_max (exact 2D, `max_distance` 60 m), clearance to the nearest building, angle between path heading and the landmark.
Report: visible %, first seen, hidden stretches, % seen within 45 deg ahead (leading lines), release points (area local minimum then +50% within 10 m),
min clearance, winding ratio (length / straight line).
Overlay on the drawing: green = A seen, blue = A only over roofs, orange = only C, red = none; dot size = isovist area.

### Heuristics it encodes (from the research, 10-12)
1. Landmark ("weenie") visible from the start and from a good share of the path. 2. Tease then reveal: a glimpse, a hidden stretch, a full reveal.
3. Compression then release: a narrow spot right before a wide view. 4. Leading lines: path heading within 45 deg of the landmark.
5. Clearance >= player width + margin (~2 m here). 6. Winding ratio 1.3-2 for a small town. Not yet coded: POI spacing 30-60 m, dead ends need a reward,
chokepoints/loops via networkx betweenness.

## Page3 result (reference numbers)
Path 117.8 m, winding 1.8. A seen 39%, first at 22 m, hidden 24-60 and 74-88 m, then in view up the hill (good tease/reveal).
C seen 80%, from the start (guides the first half). One release at 84 m = also the tightest squeeze (0.12 m to the big house under the mansion): widen there.

## Gotchas
- Camera pitch must follow the slope: aim 25 m ahead at the ground there + 2.5 m. A flat 84 deg tilt shows only hillside.
- Drawn camera arrows at the sheet edge can point off the map (page3 cam3, cam4): empty hillside there is faithful.
- pysovist: `isovist(segments (n,2,2), origin, max_distance=...)`, metrics in `.metrics` (names in `pysovist.METRIC_NAMES`); without max_distance an open view is unbounded (inf area).
- The 2D check under-counts tall landmarks and the 3D check uses one target point; read both.
- Other tools looked at: momepy (street networks), depthmapX (heavy C++), MarkovJunior / DeBroglie (generation, need .NET, not installed), Rust `wfc` crate.

## Using it on generated layouts (Avalon)
Write the generated town into the same layout.json shape (buildings as rectangles, the landmark as `mansion_A`, the spine as `path`), run step 4,
and use visible %, first-seen distance, release count and min clearance as extra scores next to the generator's own.

- page3 `path` = 16 points, 117.8 m (0.1 m/px). BUILT 10-12 as the Goobi brawler path room "Act 1b: The Hill Path" (levels.json room 2): export GLB with Blender (`-b level_blockout.blend --factory-startup -P export_page3.py -- out.glb`, drops cameras/lights) to `brawler/assets/path3d/<name>.glb` + `<name>.json` (scale, path, hill). Details: skill goobi-brawler tree/03-editor-marks.md "Path rooms".

Related: `drawing-to-building` (single buildings; its tree/04-level-map.md is the first write-up), `goobi-scan-cutout`, `sketch-concept-art`, `avalon-town-generator`.

## Reference: Drelvak's first-person Diablo Tristram (youtu.be/dhzCSubTDl8, 10-12)
Same idea from the other end: DevilutionX reads Diablo's tiles + collision grid and builds the 3D in code, so the original collision stays the truth.

## Scope

Use when the user proposes a new feature, project, engine or big rework, when choosing what to build next, when scope is growing, or when work is invisible engineering with nothing to record.

# Finish and show

Source memories: `user-goal-youtube-art` (2026-10-09) and `user-workflow-finishing` (2026-06 to 07).
Taste and fit checks for a new idea are the `project-fit-check` skill, which also has the anchor-project time system.

## The goal
- The Goobi fan games (and the other fangames) are how the user wants to **"regrow my YouTube page"** and work on their art.
- So weigh each task by two questions: **does it give a clip worth showing, and does it make them draw?**
  A playable slice, a new hand-drawn enemy or a before/after beats invisible engineering.
- When something becomes showable, say so and suggest capturing it: a screenshot key, a short clip, a before/after pair.
- Art stays hand-made (scans through `goobi-scan-cutout`); no AI voices (splice stock recordings).

## The pattern
- The user enjoys planning, sketching and ideas far more than finishing. In art that means inking and colour; in games, the last-90% grind.
  They rush the end of a piece.
- They finish fan art because recognition pulls them through, but have **never finished a game**.
- They value throughput: they chose "50 sketchy finished pieces" over "3 polished".
- The real failure mode isn't big versus small. **It's pivoting between ideas and engines before finishing**: Godot, Twine, Ren'Py, Unity, now Bevy.

## The rules to hold them to (they asked for this pushback)
1. **One small game at a time.** Ship a build someone else can play from start to end, then start the next.
2. **Scope cap: one screen.** Chosen 2026-06-16: no scrolling, no level streaming, no open world. Small arcade canon fits:
   Q*bert (cubes = dice = Daiya), Tapper (Daiya's drink-mixing streams).
   Frame a library of small finished games as a *stronger* fan project than one unfinished epic, not as settling.
3. **Get the basic loop fun before adding systems.** Don't pile speculative systems onto a working core.
4. **Near the end, favour finishing parts** (title screen, game over, saving the best score, polish) over new mechanics.
   The user said it themselves on 2026-07-23: "we just need to finish up this project before we move on towards the next one".
5. Tie the work to their strengths (design, sketching) and keep the grind parts small or tool-assisted.

## When a pivot idea comes up
- Take it seriously and say what is genuinely good about it. Then default to **"park it"** in the ideas file, not "let's build it now".
  Past examples while the Goobi RPG was close to done: an SSX-style terrain overworld, and a Klonoa-style rail side-scroller.
- If the itch persists, offer a **side test that takes hours, not a rewrite**.
- **Healthy pivots, so don't push back:**
  - The current project was deliberately finished or set down first. Goobi RPG was shelved, then Monmon Golfing started with the parked SSX hills idea.
  - **Someone specific is waiting on it.** Goobi Gooba said she'd play the game on Steam, so the user paused Monmon to finish Goobi.

- The 2026-10-09 move of all games to Bevy was the user's decision and is done. Don't reopen the engine question.
  But a later "let's try engine X" is the classic pivot; apply the rules above.

## How to say it
- Short and honest, not preachy: "Good idea; it's bigger than one screen, so I'll park it in the ideas file. Want a 2-hour test instead?"

bodies.game-fluid-sim:
---
name: game-fluid-sim
description: "Real-time game fluid sim: Barotrauma flooding, BioShock mod, SPH, shallow-water, blood-pool UE2."
---

## Scope
Real-time fluid simulation for the user's game mods - the reading list (Stam, Harris, SPH, Position Based Fluids, screen-space fluid rendering, Tessendorf, Chentanez), the Barotrauma room-and-gap model for compartment flooding, the shallow-water-with-bodies research report, the cheap blood-pool recipe for UE2 mods, and the parked BioShock flooding-mod idea. Use when the user asks about water, flooding, fluid blood or liquids in a game or mod, or says they want to mod BioShock.

# Fluids in games (and the parked BioShock idea)

Source memory: `bioshock-mod-ideas` (2026-10-05/06). Related: `hydrophobia-mod`, which has a shipped shallow-water solver and our HydroWater mod. Fluid blood was parked in `advent-mod`; the method is `old-game-mod-loop`.

## Pick the model by the effect
- **Rooms flooding, doors and breaches:** use the Barotrauma model (FakeFish, source on GitHub `FakeFishGames/Barotrauma`, non-commercial licence; read it for ideas, don't copy code into GPL work).
  - Water is a volume per room, exchanged through "gaps" by level and pressure difference.
  - Each room has a 1D spring-wave surface, plus pumps and ballast.
  - It's cheap and dramatic, and it's the practical choice for a 3D compartment mod. Hydrophobia also has per-door room levels.
- **Flowing water you wade through, waves pushing objects:** use 2D shallow water on a height-field grid, the Hydrophobia way.
  - Use HLL or Kurganov-Petrova fluxes; the report below covers coupling bodies.
- **Splashes, pours, blood spray:** use particles (SPH, or Position Based Fluids), drawn with screen-space fluid rendering.
- **Open ocean:** a Tessendorf FFT or Gerstner surface; no simulation needed. Subnautica uses Gerstner waves plus depth fog, caustics and light shafts.
- **Smoke-like or 2D gameplay fluids:** Stam's grid solver.

## Reading list
- **Grid fluids:**
  - Stam, "Stable Fluids" (SIGGRAPH 1999);
  - **Stam, "Real-Time Fluid Dynamics for Games" (GDC 2003, ~100 lines of C; start here)**;
  - Harris, "Fast Fluid Dynamics Simulation on the GPU" (GPU Gems ch. 38);
  - Crane/Llamas/Tariq, 3D fluids (GPU Gems 3 ch. 30).
- **Particle fluids:**
  - Müller/Charypar/Gross, SPH (2003);
  - Macklin/Müller, "Position Based Fluids" (2013, basis of FleX);
  - van der Laan/Green/Sainz, "Screen Space Fluid Rendering with Curvature Flow" (2009).
- **Water surfaces:**
  - Tessendorf, "Simulating Ocean Water" (2001);
  - Chentanez/Müller, "Real-Time Simulation of Large Bodies of Water with Small Scale Details" (2010).
- **Shipped games:** PixelJunk Shooter (Q-Games, GDC), Noita (GDC 2019).
- **Book:** Bridson, "Fluid Simulation for Computer Graphics" (FLIP).

## Our research (codes repo, branch `claude/hydrophobia-water-mod`)
- `games/reports/Shallow water with bodies for games.md` (notes in `research_notes/`) covers:
  - **bodies displacing water:** per-column volume stamping (Thuerey); a capped velocity coefficient (Chentanez Algorithm 2);
  - **walls:** face-based wall flags, plus Sanders/Oezgen porosity for thin walls and furniture;
  - **flux:** Kurganov-Petrova second order, with desingularised velocity `u = sqrt2·h·hu / sqrt(h^4 + max(h^4, eps))`, eps ≈ 1e-2·dx;
  - **buoyancy:** a buoyancy ramp (Cords);
  - **splash criteria:** Chentanez 0.45·g·dt/dx, dh/dt > 4, laplacian < −4;
  - **performance:** tile sleeping (Horvath); small sheets stay on CPU (a GPU 128² step is ~0.75 ms, launch-bound).
- Also `games/reports/Water detail with parallax and impostors.md` (appearance) and `games/hydrophobia-water-upgrade.md` (12-stage plan).

## Blood pools for a UE2 mod (Advent, or other UE2 games)
- 4–8 UU cells, with one explicit Euler step per frame (CFL ≈ 0.09 at 60 Hz).
- Damping `pow(1-friction, dt)`, and viscosity `H²/(H²+3·dt·ν)`.
- Sleep thresholds. Skip MUSCL, porosity and the GPU.
- Spray: particles plus screen-space rendering; pools: a floor height field.
- For the Goobi brawler, gore is ink, not blood (`gore-system`).

## BioShock (parked, not started)
- No BioShock install is known. Nothing was asked beyond "make a note of those for if I ever mod BioShock" (2026-10-05).
- Why it fits:
  - Rapture is water everywhere (leaks, floods, puddles, the ocean outside);
  - the game is a modified Unreal Engine 2.5 on D3D9/D3D10, so the UE2 script tools may partly apply;
  - water rendering would need a d3d9 proxy, like our d3d8 fork work but not d3d8to9 itself.
- If the user starts it:
  1. run the `old-game-mod-loop` research step (player complaints, what the engine exposes);
  2. check `project-fit-check` and the scope rule (one small playable change);
  3. the likely first mod is Barotrauma-style room flooding behind scripted leaks.

---

## Scope
GlmBridge - driving Golem Studio (Unreal II''s character/animation tool, GlmEd.exe) by text commands through an injected DLL and a named pipe instead of clicking its UI - the protocol (main-object commands, workspace-tree paths, win: window commands, !tree/!classes/!commands/!windows/!answer/!log), how it reaches RObject::ExecuteCommand, verified results and gotchas. Use when scripting Golem Studio, automating a 32-bit tool whose internals were mapped in Ghidra, or reviving the part-based model assembly idea.

# GlmBridge: command line into Golem Studio

Code: `C:\Users\john\Documents\github\codes\tools\C\GlmBridge\` (`src/glmbridge.c` DLL, `glm.py` client reusing helpers from `../U2EdBridge/u2ed.py`, `README.md` = the proven protocol). Commits 01fe3df, 1b6ee26 (2026-10-05). User ask: "build the golem bridge too", to drive Golem by commands instead of `golem.py`'s UI clicks, aiming at part-based model assembly. Unreal II uninstalled 2026-10-09; the pattern (find the app's own command dispatcher in Ghidra, inject, pipe text in, capture its log) works for any old tool.

## Use
`python glm.py start|exec "CMD"|run file|shell|stop`, or the `Glm` class (`start`, `attach`, `exec`, `exec_rc`, `run_script`, `stop`). `start` launches GlmEd suspended with the DLL already inside via U2EdBridge's `u2edinject.exe`, and renames `System\dxgi.dll` (BGProxy) aside for the run. Pipe `\\.\pipe\GlmBridge-<pid>`; each answer = captured log + the command's result text + `<<<GLM rc=N>>>` (1 ran, 0 not handled).

| Line | Does |
|---|---|
| `<command words>` | run on the main window's object |
| `/Folder/File.gem/Object <cmd>` or `item:/...` | run on a workspace-tree item |
| `/Folder/File.gem !commands` | that item's class-chain command table |
| `!tree [depth]` | workspace tree with each item's class |
| `!classes` | every GLM class with commands (verified: 12 classes, 104 commands, all 0-param menu actions; `_Disabled`/`_Checked` variants are state queries) |
| `win:<cmd>` | a WINDOW command on the main window (UseLastWorkspace, VssEnable, TickBackground, TexturesUseWorkspace...) via WWindow::WindowCommandf |
| `@<hwnd hex> <cmd>`, `!windows`, `!commands [hwnd]` | per-window objects |
| `!answer yes` / `!answer no` (default No), `!log` (last 64 lines), `!ping`, `!quit` | |

Verified: `/Malcolm/Malcolm.gem TotalFrameCount` runs and its box comes back as `[dialog -> OK] Total Frame Count: 1 frames`.

## How it works (from Ghidra, `u2-ghidra-editor`)
window -> `WWindow::StaticWindowGetObject` (GWL_USERDATA) -> `RObject::ExecuteCommand(CDatString&, const char*)`. Commands registered per RClass (`RegisterCommand`; SRefCmd +0 name, +0x24 param count; RClass +0x34 table, +0x38 count, +0x28 super). Log captured with `LOG_AddTarget` (ILogTarget vtable slot 2 gets each line); a MessageBox IAT hook answers dialogs. `!tree` walks RGemTreeItem children (+0x24 list head, nodes {next,prev,item}). Candidate names: `Documents\U2_research\ghidra\golem_commands.txt`.

## Gotchas
- Golem starts with NO workspace unless registry `UseLastWorkspace`=1 (set on this PC; `LastWorkspace` = U2Import.gws).
- `!quit` must answer the exit box Yes or settings don't save.
- Git Bash rewrites a leading `/` argument: use `item:/...` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`.
- Commands that open file pickers (ExportAttributes) block the bridge until the dialog is cancelled from outside.
- wsprintfA has no `*` width (crashed the first build).
- Build: `zig cc -target x86-windows-gnu -O2 -shared -o bin/GlmBridge.dll src/glmbridge.c -luser32 -lkernel32`.
- Defender quarantined u2edinject.exe until the user added the Documents\github exclusion; if it happens again the USER restores it (never touch security settings).
- Not done: the part-based assembly itself. The menu commands are all 0-param, so editing attributes or geometry by command needs more reverse engineering (CMnuItem::MnuGetCommand callers). Import still runs through `golem.py` UI automation (`u2golem`).

## Related
`glmbridge-tool` (memory), `u2golem`, `u2edbridge`, `u2-ghidra-editor`, `u2golem-importer`.

bodies.gore-system:
---
name: gore-system
description: "Engine-neutral liquid gore blueprint: three-layer split, decals, gibs, wet lens, Goobi brawler, Bevy, Advent Rising."
---

## Scope
The engine-neutral blueprint for a liquid gore system, taken from the Advent Rising mod (GORE-DESIGN.md) - goals, the three-layer split (script owns hit truth, engine decals, a renderer layer for what the engine can't draw), the feature list (hits and reactions, decals, wall runs, body streaks, goo strings, drops, footprints, hands, wet lens, gibs), budgets and the shader-cache hitch fix, settings with off switches, offline simulators and test steps, the rules kept, the to-do list, and how it maps onto the Goobi brawler as fluff/ink instead of blood. Use when designing hit feedback, blood or any persistent splat/liquid effect for a new game (Bevy, the brawler) or extending the Advent/U2 gore.

# Gore system: the reference design

Sources: `C:\Users\john\Documents\github\codes\games\advent_rising_mods\GORE-DESIGN.md` (full design; code `AdventMod/Classes/ModGore.uc`, `ModReact.uc`, `ModArmor.uc`, `ModBloodDecal`, `ModBloodDrop`, `ModPlayerBlood`, `ModSever`, `ModGib*`, `native/`; d3d8 fork `runs.hpp`, `streaks.hpp`, `strings.hpp`, `lens.hpp`, `perf.hpp`), the Unreal II port `Documents\design-refs\gore\unreal2-gore.md` (skill `u2gore`, GoreLink spec in ADVENT-GORE-HANDOFF.md). Repo `codes` is public. The Advent chat owns the live code.

## Goals (keep these for any game)
1. **Violence that reads and teaches:** a hit says where and how hard; a kill leaves a scene that tells what happened.
2. **Liquid behaviour:** sprays, pools, runs down walls and bodies, drips off ledges, stretches into strings, gets walked through, dries.
3. **Never costs a frame** (60 fps fights, no hitches).
4. **Own art only:** generated by `tools/make_*.py` or procedural in shaders.
5. **Every effect has an off switch and a budget.**

## Architecture: three layers
- **Script/gameplay** owns truth: who, where, how hard, which bone, blood kind (`BloodKind`: 0 none for robots/vehicles, 1 red humans, 2 alien purple). Places decals and actors the engine can draw.
- **Native bridge** (AdventNative.dll): `NativeCall("Blood:<cmd>")` (< 256 chars) -> the renderer's exported `U2BloodCommand` ("run", "drip", "streak", "string", "hands", "lens", "pool"...).
- **Renderer layer** (d3d8to9 fork) draws what the old engine can't: live-painted textures (pools, wall runs), extra passes over character draws (body streaks, hand blood), its own geometry (goo strings), post passes (wet lens).
In Bevy all three collapse into one ECS, but keep the split as modules: hit events -> effect spawner -> render systems.

## Features (GORE-DESIGN.md s.3)
Flinch/stagger at the hit bone + knockdowns and get-ups; death anims + ragdoll that freezes at rest; wounds (meat lumps on the nearest bone, some pulse as heartbeat spurts that paint nearby); bleed trails that clot; decals (sprays, splats, pools); wall runs; body streaks; goo strings between gib pieces; blood coat; falling drops from overhangs; footprints through fresh blood (alternating, fade with steps); blood on the player's hands/weapon; wet lens; gibs and severing. Blood dries over ~1-2 min.

## Performance
- **Compile every shader once at level load** (~0.4 s). Before: each new blood texture mid-fight compiled its own copy, 100-200 ms hitches (worst frame 283 ms -> 54 ms, 1% low 49.8 -> 56 fps).
- Live config reload only when a rule line changes (runtime switches recompiling everything caused 1.3 s freezes).
- Budgets, oldest-out: 80 decals, 48 wounds, 24 drops, 12 strings, 8 streak sources, 5 hand capsules, 6 lens drops.
- Measure: a perf line every 30 s (avg fps, 1% low, worst, frames > 50 ms) + each hitch > 80 ms with a tick stamp shared with the gore log, so hitches match events.

## Settings, testing, rules
- Settings: one ini section per subsystem with `b<Feature>` switches + size/rate/cap numbers (ModGore, ModPlayerBlood); renderer rules (`bloodrun=`, `streaks=`, `strings=`, `hands=`, `lens=`, `gloss*=`) reload live. Renderer code defaults OFF; the shipped ini turns features on.
- **Offline simulators first:** `tools/runs_sim.py`, `streaks_sim.py`, `strings_sim.py`, `lens_sim.py`, `jiggle_sim.py` draw the effect without the game; tune there, then go in game.
- Test steps (ModPilot, hidden window): HURT, SPAWN, GIBAHEAD, GOOSEVER, GOOLIST, DRIPTEST, DROPLIST, WALKBLOOD, STEPLIST; `bGoreLog=True` logs every decision. `visualqa/blood_drying.py` measures drying from prints.
- Rules: no game pixels in git/docs/video/zips; mods GPL + non-commercial (`modding-noncommercial-licences`); the FPS graph never ships on.

## Still to do (Advent)
Person playtest then tune (streak brightness, goo frequency, drying speed, run volume, lens strength); in-game menu switches + one intensity slider; 10-15 min soak test (caps hold, no slowdown, steady memory); edge cases (cutscenes, save/load mid-fight, level change, melee hand blood, purple lens drops); optional cap on stock scorch marks; rebuild the Nexus zip.

## For the Goobi brawler (2D/2.5D)
Ported 10-19 as `C:goobibrawlersrcgore.rs` + `assetsgore.json` (details goobi-brawler tree/01). Rule (user 10-19): enemies get blood and gore; Goobi only a little blood when hit, never dismemberment or gore. Keep: hit = where + how hard (flinch at the hit point, scaled splats); decal budget oldest-out; drips from overhangs; footprints through fresh splats; drying over ~1-2 min; an off switch per effect. Art: own/generated only (`goobi-brawler-sidestep`).

- Reference (user 10-20): Project Zomboid Viscera gore, video-notes tree/185: long fan of separate droplets along the swing (fall, then stick as decals), growing pool with ragged edge, stains on the hit body, blood kept through rain. Also tree/184 (2D sprite ragdolls) for fluff deaths.
## Related
`gore-system-refs` (memory), `u2gore`, `advent-rising-project`, `advent-physics-plan`, `goobi-brawler-sidestep`, `design-unreal-encounters`, `unreal2-gameplay-mod-idea` (hit feedback = top fix).

- Avalon version (10-12): `C:\avalon\reports\gore_and_destruction.md` (avalon 3f68c7b) maps this design onto Bevy + the Saturn look.
- dreamedit SDF version (10-16): the gore design ported as SDF prims + CPU sim in C:\goobi\dreamedit (src\main.rs `live`, shader blood material 4 wet->dry, lens drops in the fragment). Numbers copied into C:\goobi\dreamedit\NOTES.md "Gore numbers"; code is our own (Advent mod is GPL).

- 10-16 plasma + penetration (f47c3ec): ModGore.ShotKind by damage-type name (PlasmaTypes/BulletTypes, fixed string[8]: a config array<string> loads EMPTY without an ini key). Plasma: ModSear glow on nearest bone, blood x PlasmaBleed 0.3, no spray, gib only at 2x GibOverkill. Bullets: exit wound (ExitSpot), ExitDrops (3-8 bSpray ModBloodDrops, wall = spray mark + WallRun), PassThrough to next hostile at PenetrateKeep 0.5 within 1500. Plan/test: AdventMod/PLASMA-AND-PENETRATION.md. Pilot test: HURT n EonWeapons.dmgType_SeekerPulseFire / dmgType_HumanXJ9Fire; call test_run.ps1 with & (powershell -File flattens -Steps arrays).
- Ref 10-21 (video-notes tree/209, GMod procedural blood): lobed pools that grow, spill-over drips at edges, wall splat + one drip line, dense mixed-size spatter; keep hit puffs small.
- Ref 10-21 (video-notes tree/213 Nano Breaker): the swing direction picks the cut (horizontal/vertical/in half), each combo or weapon has its own death (hammer smears), legless enemies crawl, blood colour is a player option.

## Scope

# mm-search (built 2026-10-11)

`py -3.13 C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\llm\mmsearch.py <cmd> ...`
- `frames <video> <out dir> [every=2]`: ffmpeg, one jpg per N s at 448 px high, named `t00012s.jpg` (seconds into the video).
- `index <dir>`: embeds new/changed jpg/png/webp/bmp (+ wav/mp3/flac/ogg, untested) into `<dir>/.mmindex.npz`. About 0.1 s per image on CPU (36 frames 3.4 s, 361 frames 34 s).
- `search <dir> "text" [k=8]`: best files with cosine. **The useful mode.**
- `tag <dir> [vocab.txt] [n=3]`: writes `<dir>/tags.md`, the closest words from `mmsearch_vocab.txt` (edit it per project). Rough: only coarse scene types.
- Server starts on demand and stops at the end; `--keep` leaves it up for several calls, then `mmsearch.py stop`.

## It does not caption
An embedding model only scores how well an image matches a text. "Frames to text" here means search + tags. Speech still goes through whisper (skill video-grab). Real captions would need a vision LLM.

## Test results 2026-10-11 (X0_GDOkLKzQ news video, 36 frames)
- Search: right frame first for 5 of 6 descriptions ("pills and tablets" 0.77 vs 0.61 next, "two flowers", "github readme page", "DNA letters sequence", "chat assistant answer about a dinner menu"), second for "a game character running on a beach".
- Tags: about 7 of 12 right (UI, code page, diagram, text); misses (red pills -> "blood and gore").
- Right matches score about 0.68-0.77; non-matches about 0.60-0.65.

## Gotchas
- Request: `POST /v1/embeddings {"input":[{"prompt_string": <marker>, "multimodal_data":[<base64>]}]}`. The marker is random per server run: read it from `GET /props` `media_marker`. Plain `<__media__>` -> 500 "Failed to tokenize". OpenAI `image_url` parts are silently ignored (identical vectors), as is `/embedding` `image_data`.
- Text queries use the `task: search result | query: ` prefix; images get no prefix.
- Files: `Documents/Tools/llm/models/embeddinggemma-2-Q8_0.gguf` (309,855,456 B) + `mmproj-embeddinggemma-2-Q8_0.gguf` (554,821,024 B), ggml-org repo, Apache 2. llama.cpp build 11529 has the gemma-embedding2 arch.

1. ini / User.ini settings.

---
name: photo-fit
description: "photo_fit.py: fit a Hunyuan3D model's pose to its source photo and project the photo's colours; one-photo props"
---

## Scope
photo_fit.py - after Hunyuan3D shape + paint, fit the model's pose to the source photo (render-and-compare on the outline, then colour) and project the photo's real colours onto the visible texels. GenIA/SAM 3D Objects ideas on our 12 GB card. Usage, the full photo -> shape -> paint -> fit chain, test results, gotchas. Use when making a prop or blockout object from one photo (Avalon, Goobi, any engine).

# photo-fit (built 2026-10-11)

Why: GenIA / SAM 3D Objects (photo -> posed, photo-true objects) needs >=32 GB VRAM + Linux; our RTX 4070 Ti has 12 GB on Win10. photo_fit brings its main ideas to the Hunyuan pipeline: fit the pose to the photo, then let the photo win over the generated paint where it can be seen.

## Run
Python: `C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\Hunyuan3D-2\venv\Scripts\python` (numpy, cv2, scipy, trimesh, PIL; rembg if the photo has no alpha). CPU only, ~20-30 s.
```
photo_fit.py <photo> <painted.glb> <out dir> [res=1024] [fit=192] [project=1] [front=270|any] [transfer=0|1]
```
Full chain (example `Documents/U2Golem/photofit/hydrant/run.sh`), from `Documents/Tools/Hunyuan3D-2`:
1. `img2shape.py <photo> hi.glb full 30 octree=384 faces=60000` (GPU, ~190 s, 6.0 GB peak)
2. `paint_mesh.py hi.glb paint.glb hi_input.png faces=40000` (GPU, ~190 s, 7.1 GB peak). Give photo_fit the `*_input.png` img2shape writes (background removed, same framing).
3. `photo_fit.py hi_input.png paint.glb <out>` (CPU)

Outputs: `fit.glb` (photo-projected texture), `fit_albedo.png`, `fit.json` (pose, IoU, % texels), `sheet.png` (row 1: photo | before | after | outline overlap, red/blue = misses; rows 2-4: +90/+180/+270 before | colour match | after).

## How it works
- Pose p = yaw, pitch, roll (euler "yxz"), log scale, tx, ty, perspective, mirror. Grid search yaw front±60 step 15, pitch -30..30; 12 best by outline IoU re-scored by colour; Nelder-Mead refine.
- Projection: z-buffer visibility, weight by facing ((n_z-0.15)/0.45) and photo alpha, blurred seams, 8 px gutter fill.

## Gotchas
- **Front prior yaw 270 is needed** for Hunyuan output: an orthographic back view gives the mirrored outline, and colour alone did not separate them. `front=any` only for odd models.
- Global colour transfer (`transfer=1`) darkened results: off by default.
- Only the side seen in the photo changes (~12-14% of texels); other sides keep Hunyuan's paint.
- Pitch can drift steep (36.6 deg on a level hydrant photo) to make up for shape mismatch. Cap it if that keeps happening.
- Hunyuan paint speckle/seam dirt stays. **User 2026-10-11: that is fine, it flags the asset for the dev to replace later.**
- GPU rules (skill `local-gpu-ai`): no GPU steps while the user games; announce long runs to the other chats.

## Results
| Test | IoU before -> after | texels from photo | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| rig (`Documents/U2Golem/photofit/rig/`) | 0.642 -> 0.711 | 14% | legs + deck front closer |
| hydrant photo (`.../photofit/hydrant/`) | 0.716 -> 0.837 | 12% | grey body + nozzle restored from photo |

bodies.project-fit-check:
---
name: project-fit-check
description: "Validate game ideas against SOLAS/Myst playtime, deep-loop rules, 30-sketch scoping, and nested loop rings."
---

## Scope
Check a game idea against what the user actually plays (Steam playtime receipts - deep solo-dev puzzle games like SOLAS 128 and Myst III/IV, and narrative RPG-Maker-style story RPGs; no platformers) and against deep-loop design rules (few rules with emergent consequences, three nested loop rings, get smarter not stronger, failure gives information, the 30-sketch scoping test), plus the anchor-project time system. Use when the user weighs which project to start or prioritise, pitches a new game or mechanic, or asks if an idea is deep enough.

# Project fit check: taste receipts + deep-loop rules

Source: memory `steam-play-patterns` (from the "steam db" session, 2026-07-10, real playtime from the local Steam files). Pairs with skill `finish-and-show` (memory `user-workflow-finishing`) (loves planning over finishing, keep scope tiny) and skill `design-taste`.

## What the user plays most (hours)
SOLAS 128 ~517 (signal-routing puzzle), Third Crisis ~417 (tactical RPG/VN), Once Ever After ~396 (RPG-Maker story RPG), Myst III ~389, Warframe ~327, RimWorld ~253, Styx ~243, Love of Magic ~239 (narrative RPG/VN), Myst IV ~232, Dungeon Town ~215. Lower: Delta-V Rings of Saturn, Stuck In Time, Chains of Satinav, Thief Gold, Abiotic Factor. (Utilities like Lossless Scaling and SteamVR are excluded.) The numbers are from 2026-07; re-pull them if they matter.

Two clusters:
1. **Deep puzzle games by tiny teams**: one clever mechanic explored for hundreds of hours (SOLAS 128, Myst, Stuck In Time).
2. **Narrative story RPGs** (RPG-Maker style): ~1,600 h combined, the biggest cluster.
**No action-platformers at all.**

## How to use it
- Put the idea next to the clusters and say plainly where it fits. Ex: a Goobi point-and-click panel puzzler (Gorogoa/Moncage/Myst-like) fits strongly; a Klonoa/Pandemonium-style platformer has no precedent in the data.
- This is information, not a verdict: the user decides. Don't repeat it unasked.

## Deep-loop rules (for puzzle- or system-shaped ideas)
1. Depth = few rules with combinatorial consequences. If a new situation needs a new rule, the mechanic is shallow.
2. Three nested rings: seconds (the core verb feels good alone), minutes (the puzzle/encounter), hours (progression re-frames old elements rather than just powering up).
3. The player gets **smarter** at hour 10, not stronger (knowledge-gated: Outer Wilds, Myst, Stuck In Time).
4. Failure hands the player new information, not just a retry.
5. **Scoping test**: write 30 meaningfully different puzzle/encounter sketches from one mechanic before coding. If that's impossible, the mechanic isn't deep enough (SOLAS 128 shipped ~40 screens of one idea).

## Time and scope system
- One **anchor project** gets build time; everything else gets 30 minutes of writing-only into a parking lot (`goobi-rpg-future-ideas`-style notes).
- End each session with a one-line note for next time.
- Money: indie games are a poor effort-to-income hobby. Selling byproducts (tools/assets built along the way) fits limited hours better. The tool examples were Unity ones; after the move to Bevy they'd be Bevy plugins or assets.

## Related
Skills `design-taste`, `avalon-creative-crew`. Memories `user-workflow-finishing`, `goobi-rpg-future-ideas`, `goobi-rpg-project`, `user-goal-youtube-art`.

1. **Collage (CPU, 1 s):** `py -3.13 concept/collage.py` -> `concept/street_collage.png` (1344x896). Canvas with a horizon at y 520 and two street edges + kerbs to a centre vanishing point; `put(name, h, x, base, mirror)` pastes `cut/<name>.png` scaled to height h, bottom-centre at (x, base), multiplied onto paper so pencil stays pencil. Big near the front, small at the end of the street = depth. Copy the script and edit the `put` lines for a new scene.
2. **Paint (GPU token, skill `local-gpu-ai`; no game or Hunyuan at the same time):** `page2/concept/run.sh` has both calls:

Use when making characters look less plastic, adding skin/SSS to a D3D8/D3D9 shader layer or Bevy, tuning sssfx, or when "soft body" or "jiggle" comes up.

# Skin shading (SSS) for characters

History: memory `skin-shading-sss-notes`. Report: `codes/games/reports/Soft body deformation and skin SSS.md` (notes: `research_notes/Soft body deformation and skin SSS/realtime_sss.md`, `ue2_d3d9_feasibility.md`). Code lives in Advent: `codes/games/advent_rising_mods/AdventMod/U2Shaders/`. Unreal II is uninstalled (2026-10-09); the same shader layer (d3d8to9 fork + U2Shaders) runs Advent, so Advent is where this is live. For Bevy, the method list below carries; the HLSL does not.

## Methods (cheapest first)
| Method | What it is | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| Wrap lighting | `saturate((NdotL + w) / (1 + w))`, per-colour w (red widest) | always; free |
| Pre-integrated (Penner, GPU Pro 2) | ramp lookup by NdotL x curvature | cheap, good for faces |
| Lightwarp ramp (Valve) | 1D ramp on half-Lambert; what SFM uses | what the user means by "SFM look" |
| Screen-space SSS (Jimenez 2009/2015) | separable depth-aware blur of diffuse, masked | best quality per cost; needs a skin mask |
| Texture-space diffusion (d'Eon, NVIDIA Human Head) | blur in UV space, several Gaussians | heavy; not for these engines |
| Jensen dipole | the physics the others fake | reference only |
| Translucency (Barre-Brisebois, GDC 2011) | thickness map, light through ears/fingers | add-on |

- **Alpha blending is not scattering.** Translucent skin = light bleeding, not see-through.
- **SFM look** = VertexLitGeneric `$lightwarptexture` + `$phong` with `$phongfresnelranges` + `$rimlight`. In SFM "soft body" means jiggle bones and flexes, not a material.
- **Soft body / jiggle** = spring bones or zones (what shipped games do). Both engines hand the shader already-skinned vertices, so do springs in script first; a stateless solver can fit a vertex shader later. See the report ("Spring bones and light-warp ramps win first").

## Built in Advent
**char_skin.hlsl** (lightwarp skin as maths, close to Penner): per-colour wrap (red widest), warm band at the terminator, softened diffuse normal, ambient rim, broad oily highlight. ps_2_a, 32 constants. Writes a skin mask to COLOR1.
Rule in U2Shaders.ini: `pbr=<texture HASH> none 1 1 char_skin.hlsl` (find hashes with the texture dump/`hub` tools of the shader layer; see skill `u2testhub`).

**sss.hlsl** (screen-space, Jimenez 2015 method with its own kernel): separable blur, vs_3_0/ps_3_0, masked by COLOR1, width in world units, depth-weighted taps, per-colour profile.
```
sss=1
sssfx=<width> <strength> <falloff> <debug>    ; width ~1.2 for a face
                                              ; debug 1 = show mask, 2 = blur only
```

## Release rules
- RELEASE.md marks sss/char_skin **"Needs verdict"**: the 10-08 graphics pass was only checked in hidden pilot runs. A human must look before it ships on by default.
- JiggleSkin (SeekerSkinJ build) is local only; never ship it.
- The Gideon PBR skin rule `pbr=2e106041 gideon_uniform_pbr.dds 1.8 1.6` stays out of the release; regenerate the map with `tools\make_pbr_maps.py`.

## Tuning checklist
1. Mask first (`debug 1`): only skin lit, no armour/cloth.
2. Blur alone (`debug 2`): no halo at silhouettes (depth weighting), width in world units, not pixels.
3. Then strength; skin should look soft at the terminator, not blurred overall.
4. Compare in a lit close-up and a dark scene; the user values animation/shape over texture sharpness.

## Settled numbers (from the HLSL, 10-16; sent to Goobi dreamedit SDF editor)
SKINWRAP 0.75/0.42/0.32; skin spec pow(nh,24); rim 0.55*amb*pow(1-nv,4); SSS near w .20/.45/.62 var .020/.012/.008, far w .80/.55/.38 var .33/.12/.06, 8 taps/side at r*1.6; char_pbr f0 0.04, GGX (Karis mobile).

In a raymarcher skip the screen-space SSS pass; translucency uses SDF thickness marched along -N. Numbers and open points: `C:\goobi\dreamedit\NOTES.md`.

## Files (`C:\re\splatterhouse`)
- `zip\` holds the ISO, unpacked from `H:\Downloads-archive\Splatterhouse_Win_EN_ISO-Version.zip (moved 10-11)`. Despite the name, the disc is the Japanese release.
- `files\`: 218 extracted files. **7-Zip misreads the .bin as a CAB** (there is an embedded DirectX cab), so use `scripts\iso_extract.py` instead (strips 2352 → 2048, walks ISO9660).
- `RECON.md` (disc layout), `NOTES.md` (all findings, by phase), `names.txt` (Ghidra names), `TIPS-from-saturn.md`.
- `DISK_1\SPLATTER.EXE` (MSVC6) + `DLL6809.DLL` emulate the arcade board. **The game logic is the 6809 code in `ROMS\PRG0-7`** (8 × 64 KB), not the x86. `ROMS\OBJ.DAT` has the sprites, `SOUND\` the WAVs.

## ROM image
- The EXE loads PRG7..PRG0 into a 1 MB buffer, each file twice. Namco System 1 banking (same numbers as MAME `namcos1`): 8 windows of 8 KB.
- ROM banks 0x200-0x3FF; `scripts\mkrom.py bank_off()` turns a bank into a buffer offset (formula in NOTES.md).
- Gameplay banks: 0x230, 0x3B1, 0x3FD-0x3FF. Hit-box records are in bank 0x3B5; the enemy loop in 0x3F9/0x3FA. The sub CPU (bank 0x377) is not analysed.

## Code map (all in NOTES.md; listed so you know what exists)
- Main loop E05D → `frame_update` E17C (6-state table E1BB, indexed by DP$2A) → object loop CCDF (32 slots × 32 bytes, update table 0x8000, 25 types, roles unknown).
- Frame chain F208: players B479, scroll script EC7B, camera E480, secondary objects CD9A, enemy loop AE09.
- Actor struct (stride 0x40; players at 0x011D/0x015D, 32 enemies at 0x019D): active/hurt, invuln timer, state, state timer, already-hit flag, type, vx/vz/vy, facing, x/z/y, health, held object, hit-box frame.
- Player input: per-state handler table B501 (9 directions + 4 buttons). Jump and attack button bits and the variable jump height are in NOTES.md.

## Combat findings (Phase 3, from code, never seen in RAM)
- Units: 60 fps, 8.8 fixed point, +y down.
- **Hit test:** 3-axis box overlap (x, depth, height). 32-byte box records hold offset (x mirrored by facing), damage, x/z/y extents, a head threshold and a hit-effect id. Only frame 0 of each list matters.
- **One hit per swing:** the already-hit flag.
- **Hit reaction:** a per-type table gives the state, knockback vx/vy and a timer; dead uses its own entry.
- **Player hurt:** hurt flag plus a countdown, knockback, then invulnerability. 3 lives.
- **Physics:** gravity 0.25 px/f², terminal 8 px/f, jump -4.5 px/f, walk accel 0.25, air accel 1/16.
- **Basic melee enemy:** walks 0.375-0.75 px/f for 128 f; picks the next action at random, split by a 176 px distance; 64 f windup, then a lunge hop; contact damage from its attack box.
- The "For the Goobi brawler" table at the end of NOTES.md marks each value confirmed or guessed. Use it, not this summary, for numbers.

## Tools
-> `tree/02-tools.md` (~250t): Python 6809 disassemblers: scripts\dis.py, dis2.py (bank windows), dis6000.py; dumps go to work\ (work\p3\dis_*.txt for Phase 3).

## Phase 4 numbers (10-10, NOTES.md "Phase 4")
- Player: start health 4 (setting table E0D9: 4/6/2), 3 lives, respawn 4; hurt 16 f stun + knockback 1.0/-2.0, then 60 f invuln.
- Enemies: health = defender record byte 9 (table 0x4026); most types 1 hp, bosses 8-127 (work\p3\hp.txt). Contact damage 1.
- Player hits: punch 1, sweep 1, dive/weapons 2.

## Open (per NOTES.md) — whole game named + decompiled 10-10; open = verifying GUESS names/values
- Per-type enemy health, the default health DIP, slide attack, hit effects 2-11, the state 8 trigger.
- Exact damage numbers and invuln frame counts (box record damage byte, table B4FB) not tabulated.
- Phase 6 measured walk/jump/punch/hurt/death/enemy speeds (NOTES.md). Still open: enemy hp beyond round 1, attack-box reach, slide, later rounds.

## Sprites extracted (10-10) — local use only, never ship
- OBJ.DAT format: 2048 cells 32x32, 1 byte/px (0-15, 15 transparent); each cell = 4 16x16 quadrants TL,TR,BL,BR. Rick frame 64x64 = cells b,b+1 / b+4,b+5; Deadman 32x64 = cells b / b+4 (b = 576..).
- Palette: ROM bank 0x330 (file offset 0x60000) or 0x331, 8 records x 256 RGB; colour = pal[palnum*16+pixel]. Real palnum per sprite NOT found; palnum 0 of 0x330 is a guess.
- PNGs + full frame/cell list: C:\goobi\brawler\assets\private\splatterhouse\INDEX.md (gitignored). Rebuild: `py -3.13 -I sprbuild.py build layout.json` (tools in C:\re\splatterhouse\scripts\).
- Deadman frames are wired in as the Goobi brawler's fluff enemy (brawler/assets/art/fluff, gitignored). Animation names are eyeball guesses.

## Enemy identities (10-10)
- Sub CPU bank 0x377 draws sprites: F769 uses the class table F5FC (enemies = class 2 -> 0x63C8) -> per-type state list -> 8-byte frame records -> pieces. Details are in NOTES.md "Phase 4".
- `work\p4\rtypes.py` renders every type into `work\p4\types_sheet.png` (local only). The type→name table with confidence is in NOTES.md "Phase 4: enemy identities".
- `work\p4\rstates.py <hex,..> out.png` shows states 0..19 per type. States past a type's last real one read the next type's data.
- Stage spawn tables decoded (bank 3F8, header per round $65; 24 rounds). `work\p4\spawns.py` dumps them; round→stage table and spawn record format are in NOTES.md "Phase 4: rounds and stages". Round flow (10-10): per-round exit handlers A009[$65] set next round $6F; continue table F36D; stages 1=r1,10 2=r2-4 3=r5,11 4=r6-8,12 5=r13-19,21,22 6=r20 7=r23; r9 unused.

## Use
```
py terrain_tool.py form   sketches/alpine.json out.npy --preview out.png --masks out_masks
py terrain_tool.py form   sketches/alpine.json out.bmp --template TutA_export.bmp   # G16 for UnrealEd

```
Python: `terrain_form.form(sketch_or_dict, preset=, seed=, size=, steps=)` -> `h` (metres), `masks` (grass wet scree rock snow sand), `pads`, `score`, `formed`. Sketches: `sketches/hills|alpine|canyon|prairie.json` (coords 0..1; items ridge, valley, plateau, basin, peak, pad; `relief`, `outlet`, `roughness`, `params` overrides). -> `tree/02-pipeline.md` (~260t): 1. Rasterise the sketch to uplift (terrain_sketch): ridges raise, valleys cut corridors (the rivers), plateaus resistant (erodibility x0.05)...

Geomorphons, relative PTRM, landform share, slope PSD, slopes, Horton Rb/Rl, hypsometric curve. `terrain_refs.py fetch|stats|compare <map> <class>`: real US 3DEP terrain from the AWS elevation tiles (~24 sites, alpine/canyon/hills; tiles gitignored, `refs/stats.json` kept). - Schott's PID peak control oscillated with slow dynamics: peaks are blended in at the end instead.
- A slope cap defeats itself under the final rescale.
- Noise only for roughness (fBm gain 0.707 or FFT beta 2.0-2.2); never for the big shapes.

## Scope

## The method
1. **Beat graph.** Read the level's wiring: triggers -> events -> tagged actors (cutscenes, dialogue, scares, combat starts, doors/gates, objectives, kill-gate counters, level exit), plus the AI path network.
2. **Spine.** The critical path from player start to exit, respecting gates = the story spine.
3. **Regenerate only what's between beats** (connective spaces, combat rooms, encounters). Re-anchor the triggers and re-link the events to the new geometry so the beats still fire in order.
4. **Verify** with a pilot run (`u2autoplay` / U2Pilot): walk the path, log every event; pass only if every beat fires in the original order.
- Ship the **generator**, not modified maps: it runs on the player's own install (no game content redistributed).

## The user's rules
- **Same place, never a different-looking one.** Generated parts reuse the level's textures, mesh kit, lighting mood and scale, so the beats stay consistent.
- **Original author's voice.** Rebuild with today's craft, extend in the original writer's mindset and tone; don't bolt on a new one (the user's view of 343's Halo additions: "too dissonant").
- **Show, don't tell.** Tell beats through the space, light and staged moments; consider replaying a known event from another character's eyes (a marine, a colonist), as in the ODST Floodgate fan mod the user praised (Pvt.JonWallace). Sparse dialogue, spliced from stock lines (`design-voice-wordbank-mixing`, never AI voices).

1. **Raw blockout:** readable grey concrete volumes (big monolithic blocks and pillars, chamfered slabs, slit windows, one strong light cutting through, deep shadow, a dark corridor mouth). The user's target screenshot.

## Scope
How Unreal II mod tests were run safely beside the user's own game - the SystemBuild copy (build and test there while System is locked or in use), SystemOverride, running on a locked PC (windowed only), crash dialogs and zombie game processes, the U2Pilot environment switches, pilot gotchas, and the black-character bug as the worked example of chasing a render bug with probes until a fork fix. Use when setting up automated tests for an old game the user also plays, when a test run hangs or a crash leaves files locked, or when a character renders black/dark under a shadow.

# U2 test setup: test beside the user's game

History: memories `u2-test-copy-and-locked-pc` and `u2-black-character-bug` (both resolved 2026-10-02). Unreal II uninstalled 2026-10-09; the layout (a full copy of the game's System folder for builds and tests) is the pattern for Advent and any old game.

## Folders
- `<game>\System`: the user's own game. Install there only with the game CLOSED, `.before-<what>` backups first.
- `<game>\SystemBuild`: a full copy of System with its own Unreal2.ini (`Paths=..\SystemBuild\*.u` first, dgVoodoo windowed, probe d3d8.dll). `ucc make` runs there (System's packages are locked while the game runs). `U2PILOT_SYSTEM=<path>` makes u2pilot run from it.
- `<game>\SystemOverride` (temporary, removed 10-02): listed first in System\Unreal2.ini Paths so newer .u files win while the real ones are locked. Clean up after: move the packages into System, drop the Paths line or restore `Unreal2.ini.before-override`.
- **Trap:** SystemBuild's config can make a feature look broken that works in System (the 10-03 shadow scare, `u2-no-dgvoodoo`). Compare configs before calling a release broken.

## U2Pilot switches (tools/python/U2Pilot/u2pilot.py)
`U2PILOT_SYSTEM` (which folder), `U2PILOT_PARK=X,Y` (park the window, e.g. `-1800,60` on the left monitor), `U2PILOT_VISIBLE`, `U2PILOT_RES`, `U2PILOT_FULLSCREEN=1` (foreground only, needs the user present), `U2PILOT_LOG`. Pilot runs are pre-authorized: announce them, don't ask (`u2pilot-runs-preauthorized`). Background input: `u2input`.

## Locked PC
- Runs hang at LoadMap while Windows is locked if dgVoodoo is fake-fullscreen. Run windowed: `FullScreenMode = false` in that folder's dgVoodoo.conf (flip per run and restore).
- PrintWindow captures come out white while locked: use the game's own `shot` steps.
- The lock screen is a secure desktop: no input reaches it, even with no password.

## Crashes and zombies
- A crashed run can leave an unkillable game process that locks System\*.u and d3d8.dll until reboot (the user doesn't want restarts just for this). The fix on 10-02: the user closed its "Critical Error" dialog and it ended. u2pilot now finds that dialog and closes it itself, writing `crash.txt` in the run folder.
- Crash causes seen: "Cast of NULL to Class" in console init; TopChunk==NULL after `console SendEvent ShowMenus` from the pilot (open menus with Esc via U2Input instead); ThirdPersonMesh=None in the shadow render.

## Pilot gotchas
- The menu pauses the game: the driver needs bAlwaysTick.

# U2AutoPlay: a bot that plays like a player

Code: `C:\Users\john\Documents\github\codes\games\unreal2_mods\U2AutoPlay\Classes` (AutoPlayMutator, AutoInput, AutoBrain ~630 lines, AutoCommands, AutoAudit). Built 2026-10-07 when the user asked, away from home, for "a mod that places a simple ai to play the game". Plan and research: `codes/games/reports/Play automation and testing.md`. Unreal II uninstalled 2026-10-09; the plan is engine-neutral and is the template for Bevy test bots.

## How it works
- Load with `?Mutator=U2AutoPlay.AutoPlayMutator` on the map URL (not in User.ini). `System\U2AutoPlay.ini [U2AutoPlay.AutoPlayMutator] bStartOn`. EditPackages in Unreal2.ini and PilotRun.ini (backups *.before-autoplay).
- **Input:** the mutator swaps `PC.PlayerInput` for AutoInput, which WRAPS the previous object (Inner) so other mods' inputs keep working (U2Pilot's PilotInput; PilotDriver was changed to keep driving its own input when wrapped, they fought every 0.5 s before). It presses virtual keys, so doors, triggers, pickups and scripts see a normal player. A held key = aForward ~24000 AFTER PlayerInput processing: AutoInput sets aForward/aStrafe = 24000*x after Super/Inner, aTurn/aLookUp 0, rotation set directly.
- **Brain:** explore = nearest unvisited NavigationPoint the engine can path to (`PC.FindPathToActor`; EPathResult as byte: 0 none, 3 direct), walked waypoint by waypoint, FindRandomDest when all are visited. Fight back = any pawn whose `Controller.ControllerEnemy` (U2's renamed Enemy) is the player and in sight. Stuck (barely moved in 2 s) -> jump, strafe, Use; three stucks on one goal -> give it up. Toggles (user 2026-10-08): anything `IsUsable` for the pawn (use-triggers, buttons, lift/door movers, power stations) becomes a Use goal, remembered so it isn't spammed. 5 m visited cells for coverage.
- Console (same ExecManagers hook as `u2testhub`): `autoplay on|off|status|explore|audit`, `autoplay goto X Y Z`, `autoplay hop EVERY X Y [R]` (teleport to a random nav point within R, default 4000, every EVERY s: cheap coverage).

## Reading a run
- Every decision logs `AutoPlay:`; watchdogs log `AutoPlay: EVT <TYPE> x y z <detail>` with TYPE = STUCK, FELL (far below the lowest nav point), DIED, NOPROGRESS (no new cell for NoProgressTime), USE, HOP.
- `autoplay audit` (no play): BFS over each NavigationPoint's PathList from the node nearest the player -> `AUDIT NOREACH`, `ONEWAY` (softlock candidate), `ITEM`/`TRIGGER` with no reachable node, `ORPHANEVENT` (an Event no actor carries as Tag), `NODE`/`EDGE` (the whole network), `SUMMARY`. Doors/lifts that open later count as closed, so split levels show their later parts as NOREACH. Work is spread over frames: UnrealScript kills a call past ~1M iterations ("runaway loop").
- U2Pilot (`tools/python/U2Pilot`): `triage.py` buckets errors (Accessed None, failed to load, runaway loop, GPF..., keyed by class.function) against `triage_baseline` and fails on new buckets; `smoke.py` = every-map load run; `heatmap.py` after every run -> heatmap.png/.md (track, time-in-place, walked links, NOREACH/ONEWAY, events, coverage %).

## Status and next (plan steps)
Done: 1 triage, 2 watchdogs, 3 audit, 4 smoke, 6 heatmaps (6c6f133). Left: 5 Go-Explore (cell archive, teleport to rare/frontier cells, off-path moves for collision holes), 7 golden screenshots + a fixed-route frame-time CSV, 8 personas / record-and-mutate / an LLM supervisor that reads the log + a screenshot on stalls and sends `autoplay goto`.
Tested on Avalon TutA_Town5_Side: walks the command deck and reaches places, circled one spot (-600, 1580), never got down the tower (scripted lift progression).
Don't build: deep RL, a glitch CNN, pixel-control agents, MCTS (no fast state snapshots), raw input replay. Assert on outcomes ("reached the beat within T, no new error buckets"), never exact positions.

# U2Input: drive the game without touching the user's input

Code: `C:\Users\john\Documents\github\codes\tools\C\U2Input\` (`src/dinput8proxy.c` + `dinput8.def`, `build.bat`, `u2input.py` low-level client, `u2ctl.py` high-level driver, `probe.py` PrintWindow capture, `pilot_hold_script.txt`, `README.md`). ## How Unreal II reads input (verified)
- Mouse: DirectInput8 buffered `GetDeviceData` (buffer cap 1, ~280 calls/s). Keyboard: NOT DirectInput, window messages.
- WinDrv gates input on `GetFocus` / `GetForegroundWindow`.
- Menu pointer = WinDrv's `GetCursorPos` re-read on WM_MOUSEMOVE (not DirectInput deltas); menu clicks = DirectInput buttons. Menus only take the mouse while paused (CodeMonkey Pause).

## Recipe (pipe commands)
- `focus on`: IAT-patches WinDrv's GetFocus / GetForegroundWindow / GetCursorPos / SetCursorPos / ClipCursor and fakes Acquire. **Never touch the real device**: an earlier version let real DI acquire and the game confined the user's cursor 27 times.
- `cursor X Y` (client px, posts WM_MOUSEMOVE), `click 0`, `vkey VK` (WM_KEYDOWN/UP), `key` / `tap` DIK codes, `char` (WM_CHAR), mouse `move DX DY`.
- `u2input.py`: `focus()`, `cursor()`, `click_at()`, `vkey()`, `tap()`, `char()`, `exec(cmd)` and friends.
- **U2Ctl** (`u2ctl.py`, 2026-10-02): `exec "cmd"` (Tab opens the console line: needs `SendEvent Type` bound to Tab in User.ini; chars via `char`, then Enter), `press KEY`, `hold W 1.5`, `look DX DY`, `fire S`, `click X Y`, `run file` (script lines, `wait` included). Verified in a background run: console commands, walking, turning, firing, screenshot.
- Verified via the hook: pause-menu hover + click opens Options; wardrobe F6 / click Skaarj / third person / F6.

## U2InputHoldMouse (for the GM panel)
Export `int WINAPI U2InputHoldMouse(int on)` (faa8d55), called by the d3d8 fork's `gmpanel=1` (`u2gm`). While on, the game's DI mouse is unacquired (OS cursor free, messages reach the window), the game reads no movement or buttons (three releases first), Acquire is refused, SetCursorPos/ClipCursor are swallowed; off = reacquire on the next read. Never run in game.

   - the player re-downloads the full caption JSON (`events[].segs[].utf8`) and the hook catches it.
   Fetching the caption URL yourself returns empty (it lacks the player's pot token).
2. **yt-dlp captions** or **Whisper** when there are no captions: skill `whisper-transcribe`.
3. Old fallback: pane visible, CC on, play muted at 2x, poll `.ytp-caption-segment`.
4. No speech (music + demo): watch frames in the pane and describe what is shown; say so in the notes.

- Since 10-22 the ops study loop (skill ops-manager) re-reads these notes: Strata picks one it is curious about every 2nd cycle and writes "Curiosity: <note>" reports in Documents/Tools/ops/reports/<date>/. Keep a note's first 400 chars = title + the core idea so the pick menu reads well.

## Writing the notes
- Header: channel, title, link, length, date shared, the user's own words on why ("this was nice", "make it more cinematic").
- Then the **usable** points for the user's projects, and a "For us:" line naming which project and what to try. Not a summary of everything.
- Mark it done in the queue. Put big topic notes into the project's own doc when one exists.
- Short quotes only, no long transcript pastes.
- If the user can't remember a video, search (it took a day to find the San Andreas one: DryxioGTA, "agi has been achieved in gta san andreas").

## Scope
Offline transcription of YouTube (or any yt-dlp site) videos and local audio/video files to .txt + .srt with the user's tool in Documents\Tools\whisper (yt-dlp audio-only + faster-whisper on the CPU, int8, language auto-detected), plus the quicker yt-dlp caption download when a video already has subtitles. Use when a shared video has no captions, when the user wants a transcript of a video or recording, or when notes need exact quotes or timestamps.

# Whisper transcription (offline, CPU)

Installed 2026-10-05 in `C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\whisper\` (its own venv, Python 3.13). History: memory `whisper-transcribe-tool`. For turning videos into notes, see skill `video-notes`.

## Run
```
C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\whisper\Scripts\python.exe C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\whisper\transcribe.py <url or file> [model=small] [out=dir]
```
- Writes `<out>\<title>.txt` (plain) and `<title>.srt` (timed); default out = `Documents\Tools\whisper\transcripts\`. Prints the text path.
- Models: tiny / base / **small** (default) / medium / large-v3; bigger = slower and better, each downloaded once.
- Speed: ~3 min for a 15-min video with `small`. Run long ones in the background.
- Language is auto-detected (the Portuguese GTA videos worked); voice-activity filter is on.
- CPU only, so it needs no GPU slot and can run while the user plays or Hunyuan runs.

## Captions first when they exist (faster, exact)
```
C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\whisper\Scripts\yt-dlp.exe --skip-download --write-auto-subs --write-subs --sub-langs en --sub-format vtt -o "C:\Users\john\Documents\Tools\whisper\transcripts\subs\%(id)s" <url>
```
gives `<id>.en.vtt` (and `.en-orig.vtt` for auto captions). In-browser caption grab (no download): skill `video-notes`.

## Gotchas
- faster-whisper 1.2.1 calls `av.open(metadata_errors=...)`, removed in PyAV 15+, and old PyAV has no 3.13 wheels. transcribe.py therefore decodes the audio itself with PyAV 19 (16 kHz mono float32) and passes the array. Don't "fix" it by downgrading PyAV.
- No ffmpeg needed: yt-dlp fetches `bestaudio[ext=m4a]`, PyAV decodes.
- Music-only videos give empty or garbage text; watch those in the browser pane instead.
- Titles are sanitised and cut to 120 characters for file names.
- Transcripts are for notes and short quotes only. Don't paste long stretches back to the user (copyright).

## Where the sources disagree
- **Goal-less chatter.** [2S] calls conversations without goals weak. The game sources treat ambient barks as a deliberate layer. Rule: barks are allowed, but keep them short, few and tag-driven.
- **When to explain.** [LS] delays the big explanation for a long time (it works in long games). [2S][HF] hook fast. Rule: for short videos, ask a tiny question fast and answer it fast; for games, hoard the core secret.
- **Text in games.** [GDC, Hall] distrusts text for distracted players; [GDC, Outer Wilds] builds a whole game on found text. They agree on the principle: text works when it is optional, revisitable and under no time pressure.

## Quick checks before handing over any writing
1. What did this piece promise, and does it move that promise? [BS]
2. Who wants what here, what blocks it, and what does it cost? [LS][2S]

4. Is every lore line pulled, not pushed, and does it point somewhere? [GDC]
